verses.original: ἀδελφοί Κἀγώ οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ
verses.transliteration: adelphoi Kagō ouk ēdynēthēn lalēsai hymin hōs pneumatikois all’ hōs sarkinois hōs nēpiois en Christō
verses.literal: Brothers I vvv could not address you as spiritual but as worldly as infants in Christ

verses.original: ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα γάλα οὐ βρῶμα γὰρ οὔπω ἐδύνασθε Ἀλλ’ νῦν ἔτι οὐδὲ δύνασθε
verses.transliteration: hymas epotisa gala ou brōma gar oupō edynasthe All’ nyn eti oude dynasthe
verses.literal: vvv I gave you milk not solid food for vvv you were not yet ready [for solid food] In fact vvv vvv vvv you are still not ready

verses.original: γὰρ ἐστε ἔτι σαρκικοί γὰρ ὅπου ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστε οὐχὶ σαρκικοί καὶ περιπατεῖτε κατὰ ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: gar este eti sarkikoi gar hopou zēlos kai eris en hymin este ouchi sarkikoi kai peripateite kata anthrōpon
verses.literal: for you are still worldly For since [there is] jealousy and dissension among you are you not worldly [ Are you not ] walking in the way of man

verses.original: γὰρ ὅταν τις λέγῃ μέν Ἐγὼ εἰμι Παύλου δέ ἕτερος Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ ἐστε οὐκ ἄνθρωποί
verses.transliteration: gar hotan tis legē men Egō eimi Paulou de heteros Egō Apollō este ouk anthrōpoi
verses.literal: For when one [of you] says - I [follow] Paul and another I [follow] Apollos are you not mere men

verses.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς δέ τί ἐστιν Παῦλος διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε καὶ ὡς ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν ἑκάστῳ
verses.transliteration: Ti oun estin Apollōs de ti estin Paulos diakonoi di’ hōn episteusate kai hōs ho Kyrios edōken hekastō
verses.literal: What then is Apollos And what is Paul [They are] servants through whom you believed - as the Lord has assigned to each [ his role ]

verses.original: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ηὔξανεν
verses.transliteration: egō ephyteusa Apollōs epotisen alla ho Theos ēuxanen
verses.literal: I planted [the seed] [and] Apollos watered [it] but - God made [ it ] grow

verses.original: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων ἐστίν τι ἀλλ’ Θεός ὁ αὐξάνων
verses.transliteration: hōste oute ho phyteuōn oute ho potizōn estin ti all’ Theos ho auxanōn
verses.literal: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything but [only] God who makes [things] grow

verses.original: δὲ ὁ φυτεύων καὶ ὁ ποτίζων εἰσιν ἕν δὲ ἕκαστος λήμψεται τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον
verses.transliteration: de ho phyteuōn kai ho potizōn eisin hen de hekastos lēmpsetai ton idion misthon kata ton idion kopon
verses.literal: - He who plants and he who waters are one [ in purpose ] and each will be rewarded . . . . . . . . . according to [his] own labor

verses.original: γάρ ἐσμεν Θεοῦ συνεργοί ἐστε Θεοῦ γεώργιον Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή
verses.transliteration: gar esmen Theou synergoi este Theou geōrgion Theou oikodomē
verses.literal: For we are God’s fellow workers you are God’s field God’s building

verses.original: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ἔθηκα θεμέλιον ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων δὲ ἄλλος ἐποικοδομεῖ δὲ ἕκαστος βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ
verses.transliteration: Kata tēn charin tou Theou tēn dotheisan moi ethēka themelion hōs sophos architektōn de allos epoikodomei de hekastos blepetō pōs epoikodomei
verses.literal: By the grace - God - has given me I laid [a] foundation as an expert builder and someone else is building on [it] But each one must be careful how he builds

verses.original: γὰρ οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι ἄλλον θεμέλιον παρὰ τὸν κείμενον ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός
verses.transliteration: gar oudeis dynatai theinai allon themelion para ton keimenon hos estin Iēsous Christos
verses.literal: For no one can lay a foundation other than the [one] already laid which is Jesus Christ

verses.original: δέ Εἰ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν ἄργυρον τιμίους λίθους ξύλα χόρτον καλάμην
verses.transliteration: de Ei tis epoikodomei epi ton themelion chryson argyron timious lithous xyla chorton kalamēn
verses.literal: - If anyone builds on [this] foundation [using] gold silver precious stones wood hay [or] straw

verses.original: τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον γενήσεται φανερὸν γὰρ ἡ ἡμέρα δηλώσει ὅτι ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐν πυρὶ καὶ τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει ὁποῖόν ἐστιν ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον
verses.transliteration: to hekastou ergon genēsetai phaneron gar hē hēmera dēlōsei hoti apokalyptetai en pyri kai to pyr auto dokimasei hopoion estin hekastou to ergon
verses.literal: - his workmanship will be evident because the Day will bring it to light - It will be revealed with fire and the fire - will prove the quality . . . of each [man’s] work

verses.original: εἴ τὸ ἔργον τινος ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν μενεῖ λήμψεται μισθὸν
verses.transliteration: ei to ergon tinos ho epoikodomēsen menei lēmpsetai misthon
verses.literal: If - vvv vvv vvv what he has built survives he will receive a reward

verses.original: εἴ τὸ ἔργον τινος κατακαήσεται ζημιωθήσεται δὲ αὐτὸς σωθήσεται οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός
verses.transliteration: ei to ergon tinos katakaēsetai zēmiōthēsetai de autos sōthēsetai houtōs de hōs dia pyros
verses.literal: If vvv vvv [it] is burned up he will suffer loss - He himself will be saved - but only as if through [the] flames

verses.original: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἐστε Θεοῦ ναὸς καὶ τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ Πνεῦμα οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Ouk oidate hoti este Theou naos kai to tou Theou Pneuma oikei en hymin
verses.literal: vvv Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple and that - - God’s Spirit dwells in you

verses.original: εἴ τις φθείρει τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸν ναὸν ὁ Θεός φθερεῖ τοῦτον γὰρ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ναὸς ἐστιν ἅγιός ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἵτινές
verses.transliteration: ei tis phtheirei tou Theou ton naon ho Theos phtherei touton gar tou Theou ho naos estin hagios hymeis este hoitines
verses.literal: If anyone destroys - God’s - temple - God will destroy him for - God’s - temple is holy [and] you are [that temple]

verses.original: Μηδεὶς ἐξαπατάτω ἑαυτὸν εἴ τις ἐν ὑμῖν δοκεῖ εἶναι σοφὸς ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι γενέσθω μωρὸς ἵνα γένηται σοφός
verses.transliteration: Mēdeis exapatatō heauton ei tis en hymin dokei einai sophos en toutō tō aiōni genesthō mōros hina genētai sophos
verses.literal: {Let} no one deceive himself If any of you thinks he is wise in this - age he should become a fool so that he may become wise

verses.original: γὰρ ἡ σοφία τούτου τοῦ κόσμου ἐστιν μωρία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ γάρ γέγραπται Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν αὐτῶν τῇ πανουργίᾳ
verses.transliteration: gar hē sophia toutou tou kosmou estin mōria para tō Theō gar gegraptai Ho drassomenos tous sophous en autōn tē panourgia
verses.literal: For the wisdom of this - world is foolishness in God’s sight . . . . . . [As] it is written He catches the wise in their - craftiness

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν Κύριος γινώσκει ὅτι τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν εἰσὶν μάταιοι
verses.transliteration: kai palin Kyrios ginōskei hoti tous dialogismous tōn sophōn eisin mataioi
verses.literal: And again [The] Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile

verses.original: Ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις γὰρ πάντα ἐστιν ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Hōste mēdeis kauchasthō en anthrōpois gar panta estin hymōn
verses.literal: Therefore stop boasting in men - All things are yours

verses.original: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα πάντα ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: eite Paulos eite Apollōs eite Kēphas eite kosmos eite zōē eite thanatos eite enestōta eite mellonta panta hymōn
verses.literal: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or [the] world or life or death or the present or the future All [of them] [belong to] you

verses.original: δὲ ὑμεῖς Χριστοῦ δὲ Χριστὸς Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: de hymeis Christou de Christos Theou
verses.literal: and you [belong to] Christ and Christ [belongs to] God
